_comment: Field Assembly Market Publications. One directory per title. Each title has its own sources.json, captures/, data/, issues/ and methodology.md. Tools take --title.

lobster.name: Lobster Monitor
lobster.audience: Clients, event planners, and small buyers facing a supplier's lobster price claim.

retail_reference._comment: Read-only. Consumer direct-ship and counter observations of eight Maine sellers, published by letter; names are on the methodology page. Two records: from record_start onward, Field Assembly's own observation record at local_root (lobster/observations/, in this repository, anchored with it); before record_start, the private wedding lobster monitor, whose location is not stored here (path_env, or the gitignored path_file) and which an edition cites by name, SHA-256 and git commit. Never write to either from here.
retail_reference.record_name: Field Assembly private observation record (Maine lobster, consumer direct-ship)
retail_reference.local_record_name: Field Assembly observation record (Maine lobster, consumer direct-ship and counter), lobster/observations/

egg-butter.name: Egg & Butter Brief
egg-butter.audience: Bakeries, pastry shops, and breakfast businesses facing a supplier's price claim on eggs or butter.

BLS._comment: BLS public API v2. A free registration key raises the daily limit from 25 queries to 500 and allows up to 50 series in one request, so a title's whole BLS set is one query. The key is read from the environment at fetch time (sources.json carries the name, never the value) and is not written into any capture file. Without it the fetch fails visibly. v1 remains keyless at 25 queries per IP per day; the keyless flat files at download.bls.gov/pub/time.series have no cap but require a contact email in the User-Agent.
